1) Your vampire burns a vampire in combat. Do you get his equipment?
2) Your bleed your prey. He WWEF. You combat and superior Form of

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
aa...@sfn.saskatoon.sk.ca (Terry Wright) writes:

>Some simple questions that I just can't seem to find the answer for...

>1) Your vampire burns a vampire in combat. Do you get his equipment?

No. (unless you diablerized him in combat with Amaranth)

>2) Your bleed your prey. He WWEF. You combat and superior Form of
>Mist. Is he still eligible to block or play reaction cards with the
>vampire who WWEF?

Yes. WwEF applies until the action is ended.

>3) Can you Wolf Claws with a Melee Weapon? (Bang Nak or a Sword?)

Bang Nak - yes (it just boosts the damage done by a hand strike, per
card text).
Sword - no (it is not a hand strike - just a melee strike whose damage
is based on hand damage amount).

Messages.Author: Brian Kallenbach
Messages.Body:
Terry Wright wrote:
>
> Some simple questions that I just can't seem to find the answer for...
>
> 1) Your vampire burns a vampire in combat. Do you get his equipment?

While this would seem logical, according to the rules, when you *diablerize* someone,
you get their equipment and so on and so forth. When you burn a vampire in combat, you
don't get anything from it.

> 2) Your bleed your prey. He WWEF. You combat and superior Form of
> Mist. Is he still eligible to block or play reaction cards with the
> vampire who WWEF?

According to WWEF, that vampire may block and play reaction cards as if he were
untapped. Not having the Form of Mist card handy, I would wager that whatever happens to
an untapped vampire with Form of Mist would happen to a Waked vampire

> 3) Can you Wolf Claws with a Melee Weapon? (Bang Nak or a Sword?)

Wolf Claws apply to Hand Damage only, not Weapon Damage. A Bangh Nakh and a Bastard
Sword are both Melee Weapons, and thus, are not affected by Wolf Claws.
